When you sort GPU's by it's price/performance you notice it tends to always be worse and worse the higher you go. 

But this curve isn't always smooth - 1050 was best in price/performance among 10-series GPU, but 1060 3Gb was almost identical in price/performance while 1050 Ti was worse in price/performance vs both. So among those 3 1060 3Gb was a clear winner in terms of total performance and price/performance.

Similar story with 1060 3Gb, 1060 6Gb and 1070.  1060 3Gb and 1070 are staying closer to better part of the curve while 1060 6Gb is a worse outlier. If you wanted a card that's faster than 1060 3Gb, best deal was 1070 - not 1060 6Gb.

1650 was very poor value GPU that was worse than both 1060 3Gb and 1060 6Gb. But it's successor 1650 Super was amazing beating anything ever in price/performance even up to today in 2022.

20super gen had the smoothest curve of all. There weren't any clear outliers like in 20-series or in 10-series. 2070 Super was maybe best deal in the lineup, but the difference is a lot more subtle.

30-series are very bad in low end, but amazing in high end which is to say 30-series curve got a lot more "flatter". 3080 basically has been a king in value from this "curve" perspective.
